client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
stem: A nurse wears a disposable isolation gown for direct care of a client on Contact Precautions. What should the nurse do with the gown when leaving the client-care environment?

options.A: Remove it before leaving and discard it in the designated receptacle
options.B: Keep wearing it to care for the next client
options.C: Hang it in the room for routine reuse during later contacts
options.D: Wear it for the rest of the shift if it is not visibly soiled

rationale: CDC isolation guidance directs healthcare personnel to remove the gown before leaving the patient-care environment and states that gowns should not be reused, even for repeated contacts with the same patient. Disposable gowns are discarded; reusable gowns are handled as linen for laundering.
educational_objective: Remove a disposable isolation gown before leaving the care environment and do not reuse it for subsequent patient care.
source_document_title: Guideline for Isolation Precautions — Summary of Recommendations
source_locator: Standard Precautions, IV.B.3 Gowns > IV.B.3.a.ii and IV.B.3.b
source_claim_supported: Remove gowns before leaving the patient environment; do not reuse gowns. A disposable gown is discarded after removal.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8 / PDF p.12
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
correction_summary: Specified a disposable gown so the answer does not incorrectly imply that every reusable textile gown must be discarded rather than laundered.
audit_findings: A is consistent with removal and no-reuse guidance for a disposable gown. B–D improperly continue or reuse a contaminated gown. No second answer remains.
